27 The graph shows how the height of the water surface at a point in a harbour varies with time t as
waves pass the point.

hints: Look at arrow p: it goes from the mean height line to a point on the curve below the crest, so ask whether it shows any displacement or only the maximum displacement.
Look at the horizontal axis labelled $t$: interval q covers one complete up-and-down repeat measured in time, so decide if a time interval gives period or wavelength.
Recall that amplitude is the maximum displacement from equilibrium and wavelength needs a distance axis, neither of which matches p and q here.
walkthrough: Identify the axes: vertical is height of the water surface and horizontal is time $t$ at one fixed point in the harbour.
Define displacement as distance from the equilibrium position at any instant. Here equilibrium is the mean height, so arrow $p$ from mean height to the curve is a displacement at that time $t$.
Note that amplitude is the maximum displacement, which would reach to the crest. Since $p$ stops below the crest, it is not amplitude.

Define period as the time for one complete oscillation at a point. Interval $q$ starts when the curve falls through mean height and ends one full cycle later at the same phase, measured along the $t$-axis.
Conclude that $q$ is a time, so it is period, not wavelength, because wavelength is a length measured on a distance-displacement graph. This is option A.

A.explanation: p is the distance from mean height at one instant, so displacement, and q is the time for one full cycle on a height-time graph, so period.

B.explanation: p is correctly displacement, but q cannot be wavelength because the horizontal axis is time $t$, not distance.

C.explanation: q is correctly period, but p is not amplitude because the arrow stops part-way up the wave and not at the crest.

D.explanation: p is not the maximum value and q is not a distance, so neither amplitude nor wavelength fits a height-time graph.
